title: How Zach Yadegari built Cal AI to $1M+/month at 17 with influencer marketing
summary: Zach explains how he went from a school unblocked-games site to Cal AI, a bootstrapped calorie-tracking app doing over $1M/month. He lays out his playbook: validate virality before building, buy short-form influencer videos using RPM vs CPM math, hard paywall with a trial, then layer on paid ads using influencer creatives.

principles.text: Validate how an idea will go viral on social media before building it.
principles.quote: it's making sure that we know how we're going to blow it up if we have a product that we think this is a really cool product but there's nothing to tap into on social media no Niche no influencer to promote it it's going to be 10 times harder

principles.text: Influencer deals must be profitable: revenue per 1,000 views (RPM) must exceed cost per 1,000 views (CPM).
principles.quote: every dollar you pay per thousand views needs to be less than the amount of money you will make per thousand views

principles.text: Pay influencers upfront based on predicted views, and bundle several videos on retainer to bring the price down.
principles.quote: we'll do four videos with you we'll pay upfront all the money for them and that's usually one of the main tactics we do to actually get the price down a lot

principles.text: Make sponsored integrations seamless so they don't feel like ads.
principles.quote: We make the integration super super seamless where people don't even know it's an ad

principles.text: Outreach is a numbers game; most people quit after 100 DMs and never negotiate creatively.
principles.quote: people give up after dming 100 influencers you have to DM thousands

principles.text: Hard paywall utility apps with a free trial instead of going free with ads or a premium upgrade.
principles.quote: people shouldn't be scared to just hard pay wall and not let anyone use the app without paying upfront
